original_poem:
கண்ணே களிமணே, கன்னியே, 
பொண்ணே பொன்னாதக் குழந்தை,
பாலகமுது சுகம் தரும் மதி மாலையே,
பறவைகளின் குரல் சொல்லும் மதியம்
அன்றென்று நினைவினில் அழுதிருக்கிறேன்.
translated_poem:
O beautiful-eyed girl,
Golden child, beloved one,
You are the nectar of happiness,
Your voice a bird's song in the afternoon
In memories past, I weep.

stanzas.loss_note: பாலகமுது (pālakamudhu) compounds 'child' with 'amudhu' (nectar/ambrosia), a term carrying deep devotional and Sangam resonance for the sweetness of a beloved; 'nectar of happiness' loses the child-specific tenderness encoded in the compound.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the child as pure, yielding clay of the speaker's joy
the child's presence as a moonlit evening of sweetness now lost
birdsong-filled afternoons as the sensory vessel of irretrievable memory

cultural_entities.translation_note: Amudhu (அமுது) is the Tamil word for divine nectar used in devotional and Sangam poetry; its compound with 'child' is flattened to 'nectar of happiness'.
